subject: Helius Health — request to tailor uptime exhibit + operational rollback language
messages:
From: Jamal Reynolds <jamal.reynolds@heliushealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Cho <mcho@heliushealth.com>, procurement@heliushealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tailored uptime exhibit for enterprise MSA

Sergio —

Thanks for the intro last week. Procurement and our platform team reviewed the standard MSA/SLA and we have two items we need Redwood to consider before we can proceed to signature:

1) Uptime target: our security team is pushing for 99.99% availability for the production inference path (model-serving APIs). We understand this is above standard hosted tiers — can Redwood provide a tailored availability exhibit (order form language) with a clear credit matrix if we meet & miss?

2) Operational rollback / migration triggers: because we operate in a clinical workflow, we need a narrow clause that allows a controlled rollback to our last-known-good provider if latency or correctness regressions persist. Suggested trigger: sustained P99 latency > 700ms for > 72 continuous hours or repeated outages totaling > 2 hours in a 24-hour window. We also need a commitment on evidence (latency exports and request-level audit logs) to validate triggers.

Attached is an initial redline file with our team's requested edits to the uptime exhibit and order form language. Our target is to finalize commercial and legal language by next week (procurement window). Can you confirm feasibility and approximate timeline?

Appreciate it — Jamal

--
Jamal Reynolds
Director, Procurement
Helius Health
jamal.reynolds@heliushealth.com
+1 415-555-0149

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamal Reynolds <jamal.reynolds@heliushealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tailored uptime exhibit for enterprise MSA

Jamal — thanks for the clear notes and for attaching the redlines. Short answer: we can get close to what you're asking but need to align on exact metric definitions and operational playbooks. Quick clarifying questions to help us scope:

- Which endpoints are in-scope for the 99.99% ask (inference API / embeddings / batch infer)?
- What steady-state QPS and burst profile should we size for (typical p95/p99 latencies depend heavily on request size and concurrency)?
- For rollback triggers, are you expecting a hard automatic failover (we cut traffic) or a contractual right to revert (manual migration / operational assistance)?

Plan: I'll loop in Grace (Customer Success for oncall/runbook expectations) and Neha (solutions/legal for evidence & order form wording). We will review the redlines, propose alternative language for the order form and exhibit that preserves operational controls, and return a signature-ready order form + DocuSign link. Expect a draft by end of day Tuesday PST.

If you can send an example traffic profile (QPS, avg tokens, peak hours) that will speed things up.

Thanks — Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Office: +1 510-555-0212

From: Jamal Reynolds <jamal.reynolds@heliushealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Cho <mcho@heliushealth.com>, procurement@heliushealth.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tailored uptime exhibit for enterprise MSA

Sergio —

Thanks for the quick reply. In-scope: the production inference REST endpoints (real-time text-gen) only — not embeddings or async batch. Typical production profile: 40 RPS steady, 120 RPS burst for 10-15 minutes, average request ~120 tokens.

On rollback: we are seeking a contractual right to initiate a controlled rollback if the metrics threshold is met and Redwood can't remediate within a defined window. We don't expect automatic cutover; we want the ability to fail traffic to a prior provider with Redwood's operational assistance. The language in our redlines attempts to capture a 72-hour contiguous threshold for the P99 latency and a 2-hour total outage within 24 hours threshold.

Attached is the redlines doc (updated with the traffic profile). Please review and propose Redwood's preferred fallback language. We also need Redwood to commit to delivering monthly latency exports and 30-day request-level audit logs for the production tenancy as part of the evidence package.

Best,
Jamal

To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 June 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Helius request — uptime exhibit & rollback clause (notes)

Team — quick internal notes based on Jamal's redlines and traffic profile. Key constraints and options: 

1) Feasibility: 40 RPS steady / 120 RPS burst (avg 120 tokens) is within Dedicated pool sizing, but hosted tier at standard instance sizes will need a quantization/replica set to hit p99 targets. Dedicated or Private deployment will make 99.99% realistic; hosted can be close but we should avoid an absolute 99.99 guarantee without capacity reservation.

2) Alternative proposal for the exhibit:
  - Keep availability target at 99.95% for hosted; offer a Dedicated SLA for 99.99% (reserved capacity in order form).
  - Define latency SLAs as measurement commitments (p50/p95/p99) rather than a single numeric P99 threshold tied to rollback. Example: p95 < 220ms, p99 < 550ms (measured at edge egress in customer's region) with an explicit measurement method and sample rate.
  - For rollback triggers: replace "automatic cutover" language with an "operational remediation window" clause — Redwood will have 72 hours to remediate after verified evidence; if remediation fails, client may initiate a coordinated rollback with support for data/export and routing guidance. That gives Redwood time to fix transient infra issues while preserving Helius's ability to recover.

3) Evidence and auditability: we can export daily latency histograms and a selectable 30-day request log (redacted for PII) and provide a monthly evidence package. We should offer an SLA addendum appendix listing what is produced (csv of percentiles, sample traces, request-ids). I'd attach a sample metrics export (evidence_latency_metrics.csv) to show format.

4) Commercial: if Helius wants 99.99 on prod we should price Dedicated reservation (3x baseline cost) and include a standard credit matrix for downtime/latency breaches. Provide a fallback credit that scales with severity and duration.

Action items: Aditya — can you confirm operational runbook language we would commit to for the 72-hour remediation window and the data we can deliver? Neha — please propose order form/redline language for the Dedicated offer and a credit schedule. Grace — please outline onboarding steps and a rollback playbook (roles, contacts, expected timelines).

Thanks — Sergio

[Attachment: evidence_latency_metrics.csv]
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamal Reynolds <jamal.reynolds@heliushealth.com>
Cc: Maya Cho <mcho@heliushealth.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 03 June 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Helius — proposed SLA exhibit & signature-ready order form link

Jamal —

Appreciate the traffic profile and clear redlines. We've reviewed internally and propose the following path forward:

1) Offer: Dedicated production pool (order form) with a 99.99% availability exhibit and latency commitments scoped to the inference REST endpoints you specified. Latency example: p95 < 220ms, p99 < 550ms (measured per the exhibit measurement appendix).

2) Rollback / remediation language: Redwood will commit to a 72-hour remediation window after a verified breach. If remediation is not completed in that window, Helius may initiate a coordinated rollback; Redwood will provide data exports, request-level logs (redacted as needed), and an engineering contact to assist the migration. We replaced automatic cutover language with this coordinated rollback + remediation window that meets both operational safety and procurement needs.

3) Evidence package: monthly percentile exports and a selectable 30-day request-log extract; we will produce a one-time onboarding export to establish baselines.

4) Commercial: 99.99% availability and the latency guarantees require Dedicated reserved capacity. I've prepared a signature-ready order form for the Dedicated pool and an attached SLA exhibit with the measurement appendix.

Please review the attached updated exhibit and order form. If this aligns, accept via DocuSign here: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC1234567. Once signed, we will schedule a short onboarding call (Grace will coordinate) and begin standby capacity provisioning.

If you'd like, we can also add a 30-day trial of priority incident handling during the initial window to increase confidence.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
